text:
Marco: hey folks — quick spotcheck: we got a small 504 blip starting ~10:02 from ingress path `/v1/generate` mostly for tenant `alpha`. where's the quickest place to get traces + per-tenant 4xx/5xx breakdown? want to propose a short debounce window if noise.

Priya: ping @Jules in case runtime wants to weigh in. For dashboards: Grafana -> 'Ingress Errors by Route' has tenant filter. Link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ingress-errors (add ?var-route=%2Fv1%2Fgenerate&var-tenant=alpha). For traces use Trace UI -> search `request.path:"/v1/generate" AND http.status_code:504 AND tenant:alpha`.

Jules: ops-bot shows the alert fired. Short answer: use the route+tenant heatmap dash + the sample traces panel. Quick log query you can run: `project=prod | json | where path=="/v1/generate" and status==504 | summarize count() by bin(1m), tenant`.

ops-bot: ALERT PROD_504_SPIKE fired for route `/v1/generate` (30s window). Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.com/prod-504-spike — please collect 3 sample traces and cpu/mem at alert time.

Sam: if this is noisy, I usually propose changing the alert window to 5m and require >2x baseline for that tenant. baseline = median over last 1h for tenant. Also check upstream proxy timeouts (nginx) and look for 504 in proxy logs. quick curl to reproduce header context: `curl -v -H 'X-Tenant: alpha' https://ingress.redwood.com/v1/generate`.

Marco: thanks — i'll pull traces now and propose debounce 5m x2-baseline in the alert PR. i'll attach one sample trace and the heatmap link.

Priya: also check kvcache timeout metric `kvcache.timeout{route="/v1/generate"}` — sometimes kvcache evictions cascade into short 504 bursts.

Jules: when you open the alert PR, tag @Jules and @eng-runtime. small note: add `suppress_for` in the policy (so alerts don't reopen on short flaps) rather than only shortening the rule window. :thumbsup:

Marco: ack, will do. thanks everyone :pray:
